genes/ECOLI/lptE/lptE-ai-review.yaml.description: LptE (formerly RlpB, "rare lipoprotein B") is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein of Escherichia coli and the plug subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It is triacylated at its N-terminal cysteine and delivered to the inner leaflet of the outer membrane by the Lol pathway. About three quarters of LptE sits inside the lumen of the 26-stranded LptD beta-barrel, forming a two-protein plug-and-barrel complex in 1:1 stoichiometry. LptE has two roles. First, it is needed for LptD biogenesis: it engages LptD while BAM assembles it, stabilizes the barrel, and drives the disulfide rearrangement that yields functional, correctly oxidized LptD. Second, it binds LPS directly through conserved basic surface loops and can disrupt LPS-LPS interactions, which may help LPS insertion into the outer leaflet. Depletion of LptE stops newly made LPS from reaching the cell surface, raises outer-membrane permeability, and is lethal. Accessory lipoproteins LptM and LptY associate with the translocon and modulate LptD conformation and the stability of its connection to the periplasmic bridge.

interpro/panther/PTHR45772/PTHR45772-rev.preferred_name: LivG/LivF/LptB-type ABC transporter ATP-binding protein family
interpro/panther/PTHR45772/PTHR45772-rev.summary: This ABC nucleotide-binding-domain family includes both amino-acid uptake motors and LptB-like lipid-extraction motors. ATP binding/hydrolysis and coupling to membrane partners are conserved, while transported cargo depends on the specific paralog and assembly. Characterized E. coli LptB and related LPS-system motors energize LptFG extraction rather than themselves carrying LPS through a bilayer. SF10 distinguishes the LptB-like group from Liv/Bra amino-acid ATPases, but also contains homologs from non-LPS-producing organisms and therefore does not establish native LPS cargo by itself.
interpro/panther/PTHR45772/PTHR45772-rev.coherence_reason: Amino-acid uptake groups and LptB-like SF10 have different partner/substrate roles. SF10 includes the reviewed E. coli/KT2440 LptB proteins together with Thermotoga TM1054/Q9X0E4 and Deinococcus DR_2134/Q9RSJ0. Thus both family-wide and unqualified SF10-wide LPS transport claims exceed the current evidence. ATPase activity remains a conserved genus, not a complete cargo-selective transporter function.

interpro/panther/PTHR30189/PTHR30189-rev.summary: LptD proteins form the outer-membrane barrel and periplasmic entry domain of characterized bacterial LPS transport systems. # lptA (Q88P98) notes

P. putida KT2440 lptA is the orthologue of E. coli K-12 lptA (both in PANTHER PTHR36504:SF1).
All GOA rows for this entry are electronic (IEA). Each row is supported by curated text from this entry's
UniProt record (HAMAP-rule statements or family/domain signatures; ARBA-only statements are not cited) and
by experimental quotes on the E. coli orthologue, reused from `genes/ECOLI/lptA/lptA-ai-review.yaml`.
No provider deep research was run for this gene.

## UniProt statements quoted

- `May form a bridge between the inner membrane and the outer membrane, via interactions with LptC and LptD, thereby facilitating LPS transfer across the periplasm.`
- `Required for the translocation of LPS from the inner membrane to the outer membrane.`
- `SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Periplasm`
- `TIGR03002; outer_YhbN_LptA`

## E. coli literature cited

- PMID:17056748, PMID:18424520, PMID:18480051, PMID:20446753, PMID:20720015, PMID:22668317, PMID:29449493

## History

- 2026-11-02: support added to every row and core function; correct-but-general terms changed to MODIFY;
  methods-only quotes dropped; notes rewritten to list this review's own decisions (PR #5365 review rounds).

P. putida KT2440 lptB is the orthologue of E. coli K-12 lptB (both in PANTHER PTHR45772:SF10).

## E. coli literature cited

- PMID:19500581, PMID:24639492, PMID:27795402, PMID:29449493, PMID:30894744

## Decisions in this review

- GO:0000166 nucleotide binding (IEA): MODIFY to GO:0005524 ATP binding.
- GO:0005524 ATP binding (IEA): ACCEPT.
- GO:0005737 cytoplasm (IEA): KEEP_AS_NON_CORE.

## History

- 2026-11-02: support added to every row and core function; correct-but-general terms changed to MODIFY;
  methods-only quotes dropped; notes rewritten to list this review's own decisions (PR #5365 review rounds).

All 7 original ordered annotation rows were reviewed. Their machine payloads, actions and historical NEW lifecycle are retained; no new annotation was added. The prior note about no provider attempt is historical: an actual Falcon run now failed HTTP 403, archived under `.cache/module-audit-logs/lps-20261107/psepk-consultation/falcon-lptB.log`; no provider report was fabricated.

PAINT-loss traversal could not be resolved because the exact KT2440 accession is absent from the cached family tree. The tool footer is not evidence of an independently established absence of loss. These original rows are IEA (and retained historical ISO proposals for LptD/E), not IBA.

KT2440 biological roles are inferred from its own specialized signatures and curated rule-supported statements plus source-scoped homolog experiments. P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC structures and heterologous expression do not become KT2440 assays. Generic ABC identity is insufficient to specify LPS. The A/C bridge transfer, B ATPase motor, F/G cargo-cavity contributions and D/E outer-membrane translocation are distinct functional claims.

PMID41407669 supplies structural/biochemical evidence for PAO1-LAC LptB2FG(C), not a target assay. Its discussion of Pa-LptC failure to substitute E. coli LptC cites prior studies and concerns partner compatibility; no native LptC role loss or universal cross-species compatibility follows. No assay-specific residue rule or partial-complementation magnitude is transferred.

Relevant source findings:

- [PMID:19500581] The E. coli biochemical study reports LptF/LptG association with LptB and inclusion of LptC. Complex association supports subunit assignments but is not itself a complete transport-flux assay. Verbatim: "We report here that both LptF and LptG formed a complex with LptB."
- [PMID:24639492] E. coli LptB nucleotide-state structures and activity/function measurements distinguish ATP hydrolysis from productive coupling to LPS transport. Verbatim: "Our studies establish the essentiality of ATP hydrolysis by LptB to power LPS transport in cells"
- [PMID:27795402] E. coli LptB2FG mutational work examines coupling of ATP hydrolysis to extraction; exact residue phenotypes are not assigned to KT2440 without sequence/construct verification. Verbatim: "The LptB2FG proteins form an ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter that uses energy from ATP hydrolysis in the cytoplasm to facilitate extraction of LPS from the outer face of the cytoplasmic membrane prior to transport to the cell surface."
- [PMID:29449493] Purified E. coli Lpt components reconstitute ATP-dependent membrane-to-membrane LPS movement. Necessity/sufficiency refers to the tested assembled seven-protein system, not autonomous transport by every component. Verbatim: "Thus, all seven Lpt proteins and ATP are necessary and sufficient for membrane-to-membrane transport to occur."
- [PMID:30894744] E. coli K-12 lpt genes expressed in BL21(DE3) support nanodisc structural and ATPase analyses of LptB2FG(C); the structures resolve an LPS-binding cavity and coupling. These are homolog experiments for KT2440. Verbatim: "Six lipid acyl chains of LPS tightly fit into a cone-shaped hydrophobic pocket formed by TMs 1, 2, and 5 of LptF and LptG"
- [PMID:18424520] E. coli localization and depletion distinguish cytoplasmic LptB, membrane-anchored LptC and periplasmic LptA within one LPS-assembly pathway. Verbatim: "Thus, we have identified an essential LPS transport component in every cellular compartment: LptB in the cytoplasm, LptC in the IM, LptA in the periplasm, and LptD and LptE in the OM."
- [PMID:41407669] P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC genes expressed in E. coli support structural/biochemical characterization of LptB2FG(C); tagged LptB variants partly complement a P. aeruginosa conditional mutant. The reported Pa-LptC/Ec-LptC incompatibility cites earlier work and concerns assembly compatibility, not loss of the native LptC role. No KT2440 assay is presented. Verbatim: "each gene (lptB, lptC, lptF and lptG) had been amplified from P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC genomic DNA (47085D-5 ATCC) using PCR"

original_text.genes/PSEPK/lptC/lptC-notes.md:
# lptC (Q88P97) notes

P. putida KT2440 lptC is the orthologue of E. coli K-12 lptC (both in PANTHER PTHR37481:SF1).
All GOA rows for this entry are electronic (IEA). Each row is supported by curated text from this entry's
UniProt record (HAMAP-rule statements or family/domain signatures; ARBA-only statements are not cited) and
by experimental quotes on the E. coli orthologue, reused from `genes/ECOLI/lptC/lptC-ai-review.yaml`.
No provider deep research was run for this gene.

## UniProt statements quoted

- `Facilitates the transfer of LPS from the inner membrane to the periplasmic protein LptA.`
- `SUBCELLULAR LOCATION: Cell inner membrane`
- `TIGR04409; LptC_YrbK`

## E. coli literature cited

- PMID:16765569, PMID:20720015, PMID:29449493, PMID:30894744

## Decisions in this review

- GO:0005886 plasma membrane (IEA): ACCEPT.
- GO:0015920 lipopolysaccharide transport (IEA): ACCEPT.
- GO:0017089 glycolipid transfer activity (IEA): MODIFY to GO:0140332 lipopolysaccharide transfer activity.
- GO:0030288 outer membrane-bounded periplasmic space (IEA): ACCEPT.
- GO:0043165 Gram-negative-bacterium-type cell outer membrane assembly (IEA): ACCEPT.
- GO:0046836 glycolipid transport (IEA): MODIFY to GO:0015920 lipopolysaccharide transport.
- GO:0140332 lipopolysaccharide transfer activity (IEA): ACCEPT.
- Core function: enables GO:0140332 lipopolysaccharide transfer activity; processes GO:0015920, GO:0043165.

## History

- 2026-11-02: support added to every row and core function; correct-but-general terms changed to MODIFY;
  methods-only quotes dropped; notes rewritten to list this review's own decisions (PR #5365 review rounds).

## 2026-11-07 independent LPS module consultation

All 7 original ordered annotation rows were reviewed. Their machine payloads, actions and historical NEW lifecycle are retained; no new annotation was added. The prior note about no provider attempt is historical: an actual Falcon run now failed HTTP 403, archived under `.cache/module-audit-logs/lps-20261107/psepk-consultation/falcon-lptC.log`; no provider report was fabricated.

PAINT-loss traversal could not be resolved because the exact KT2440 accession is absent from the cached family tree. The tool footer is not evidence of an independently established absence of loss. These original rows are IEA (and retained historical ISO proposals for LptD/E), not IBA.

KT2440 biological roles are inferred from its own specialized signatures and curated rule-supported statements plus source-scoped homolog experiments. P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC structures and heterologous expression do not become KT2440 assays. Generic ABC identity is insufficient to specify LPS. The A/C bridge transfer, B ATPase motor, F/G cargo-cavity contributions and D/E outer-membrane translocation are distinct functional claims.

PMID41407669 supplies structural/biochemical evidence for PAO1-LAC LptB2FG(C), not a target assay. Its discussion of Pa-LptC failure to substitute E. coli LptC cites prior studies and concerns partner compatibility; no native LptC role loss or universal cross-species compatibility follows. No assay-specific residue rule or partial-complementation magnitude is transferred.

Relevant source findings:

- [PMID:16765569] E. coli conditional expression and complementation establish essentiality of the yrbK/lptC-containing distal locus under the tested conditions; this is pathway-context evidence, not a direct KT2440 LPS-transfer assay. Verbatim: "the three distal genes (yrbK, yhbN and yhbG) are essential for E. coli viability."
- [PMID:18424520] E. coli localization and depletion distinguish cytoplasmic LptB, membrane-anchored LptC and periplasmic LptA within one LPS-assembly pathway. Verbatim: "Thus, we have identified an essential LPS transport component in every cellular compartment: LptB in the cytoplasm, LptC in the IM, LptA in the periplasm, and LptD and LptE in the OM."
- [PMID:20720015] E. coli LptC binds LPS and transfers it directionally to LptA; cysteine-accessibility experiments orient its soluble domain toward the periplasm. Verbatim: "In vitro, LptA can displace lipopolysaccharide from LptC (but not vice versa), consistent with their locations and their proposed placement in a unidirectional export pathway."
- [PMID:29449493] Purified E. coli Lpt components reconstitute ATP-dependent membrane-to-membrane LPS movement. Necessity/sufficiency refers to the tested assembled seven-protein system, not autonomous transport by every component. Verbatim: "Thus, all seven Lpt proteins and ATP are necessary and sufficient for membrane-to-membrane transport to occur."
- [PMID:30894744] E. coli K-12 lpt genes expressed in BL21(DE3) support nanodisc structural and ATPase analyses of LptB2FG(C); the structures resolve an LPS-binding cavity and coupling. These are homolog experiments for KT2440. Verbatim: "Six lipid acyl chains of LPS tightly fit into a cone-shaped hydrophobic pocket formed by TMs 1, 2, and 5 of LptF and LptG"
- [PMID:41407669] P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC genes expressed in E. coli support structural/biochemical characterization of LptB2FG(C); tagged LptB variants partly complement a P. aeruginosa conditional mutant. The reported Pa-LptC/Ec-LptC incompatibility cites earlier work and concerns assembly compatibility, not loss of the native LptC role. No KT2440 assay is presented. Verbatim: "each gene (lptB, lptC, lptF and lptG) had been amplified from P. aeruginosa PAO1-LAC genomic DNA (47085D-5 ATCC) using PCR"

# lptE (P0ADC1) notes

Review session 2026-10-24. No provider deep research was run (no `*-deep-research-*.md`); the review relies on the cached publications and the UniProt entry.

## Sources used
- UniProt P0ADC1 (`lptE-uniprot.txt`): lipid-anchored outer-membrane lipoprotein; binds LPS; required for LptD assembly.
- Discovery as RlpB partner of Imp/LptD [PMID:16861298 "Because RlpB does not function simply to stabilize or target Imp, we conclude that both of these proteins function together in what is likely to be the last step in LPS assembly, localization to the outer leaflet of the OM."]
- 1:1 complex, LPS binding [PMID:20203010 "We also demonstrate that LptE binds LPS specifically and may serve as a substrate recognition site at the OM."]
- Direct LPS binding and disaggregation, crystal structure [PMID:24938785 "Our results establish that LptE binds LPS specifically and that this is crucial to LptE’s function in vivo."]
- Plug inside the LptD barrel [PMID:21257904]; required for BAM-dependent LptD assembly [PMID:21257909, fetched]; disulfide-rearrangement checkpoint [PMID:26370939]; LptM [PMID:37821449]; reconstitution [PMID:29449493].

## Decisions
- LPS binding (IBA and IDA): ACCEPT. Core MF, plus NEW contributes_to GO:0015221 (the activity belongs to the LptDE complex).
- 5 bare protein-binding rows: REMOVE.
- outer membrane: MODIFY to cell outer membrane.
- GO:1990351: IBA and IDA (PMID:29449493) rows both MODIFIED to GO:0062051, same handling as lptD and lptB; core in_complex is GO:0062051. No validator warning remains.


## 2026-11-07 — cross-taxon Lpt audit, E. coli member consultation

All original annotation rows, reference findings and core roles were reassessed. Source payloads/order, qualifiers and historical NEW lifecycle remain unchanged. Targeted full-primary reading supports the existing division between LptB ATPase, membrane extractor subunit contributions, bridge transfer and terminal LptDE translocation. The normal PAINT-loss check reports no IRD/IKR loss on this target lineage; this is not a whole-family uniformity claim. description: >-
  LptE (formerly RlpB, "rare lipoprotein B") is an essential outer-membrane lipoprotein of Escherichia
  coli and the plug subunit of the LptDE lipopolysaccharide (LPS) translocon. It is triacylated at its
  N-terminal cysteine and delivered to the inner leaflet of the outer membrane by the Lol pathway. About
  three quarters of LptE sits inside the lumen of the 26-stranded LptD beta-barrel, forming a two-protein
  plug-and-barrel complex in 1:1 stoichiometry. LptE has two roles. First, it is needed for LptD biogenesis:
  it engages LptD while BAM assembles it, stabilizes the barrel, and drives the disulfide rearrangement
  that yields functional, correctly oxidized LptD. Second, it binds LPS directly through conserved basic
  surface loops and can disrupt LPS-LPS interactions, which may help LPS insertion into the outer leaflet.
  Depletion of LptE stops newly made LPS from reaching the cell surface, raises outer-membrane permeability,
  and is lethal. Accessory lipoproteins LptM and LptY associate with the translocon and modulate LptD
  conformation and the stability of its connection to the periplasmic bridge.

# NEIMB/lptE manual review notes

## 2026-11-07 audit

All 4 seeded rows retained in order; no NEW annotation proposed. Real Falcon research failed HTTP403 authentication; no provider report was fabricated. Primary PMID21705335 was read from an externally acquired full PMC source while its normal abstract cache remains unchanged. The H44/76 natural CDS identity bridge is exact, but does not relabel native H44/76/HB-1 phenotypes as MC58 experiments.

Support LptD biogenesis or stability through physical association at the outer membrane; inferred for MC58 from its exact natural sequence match to H44/76 LptE and native H44-derived association/deletion/complementation evidence. The available experiments do not establish autonomous foldase activity or an obligatory LPS-translocation contribution.

Normal PAINT-loss check found no IRD/IKR on the target lineage. This is not an independent proof of every propagated function. LptE association is demonstrated with His-tag and untagged/BamA controls; gross electrophoretic folding differences do not establish an autonomous generic refolding activity.

Evidence, preserved source hashes, ontology snapshots and validation are in analysis/module_audits/bacterial_lps_transport/neisseria-consultation/.

# NEIMB/lptH manual review notes

## 2026-11-07 audit

All 9 seeded rows retained in order; no NEW annotation proposed. Real Falcon research failed HTTP403 authentication; no provider report was fabricated. Primary PMID21705335 was read from an externally acquired full PMC source while its normal abstract cache remains unchanged. The H44/76 natural CDS identity bridge is exact, but does not relabel native H44/76/HB-1 phenotypes as MC58 experiments.

Transfer LPS through the periplasm as the LptA-family bridge carrier. This molecular role is inferred from specific architecture and characterized LptA homologs, reinforced by exact natural H44/76 sequence identity and source-strain surface-delivery defects; purified MC58 transfer kinetics are not available.

LptH is the literature carrier name; UniProt calls NMB0355 lptA. It is not the unrelated lipid A phosphoethanolamine transferase. PAINT PTN002194456 supports the LptA lineage; normal loss check found no applicable IRD/IKR. Carrier MF remains an explicit mechanistic inference, not purified target kinetics.

Evidence, preserved source hashes, ontology snapshots and validation are in analysis/module_audits/bacterial_lps_transport/neisseria-consultation/.

original_text.genes/NEIMH/lptD/lptD-notes.md:
# NEIMH/lptD manual review notes

## 2026-11-07 audit

All 6 seeded rows retained in order; no NEW annotation proposed. Real Falcon research failed HTTP403 authentication; no provider report was fabricated. Primary PMID21705335 was read from an externally acquired full PMC source while its normal abstract cache remains unchanged. The H44/76 natural CDS identity bridge is exact, but does not relabel native H44/76/HB-1 phenotypes as MC58 experiments.

Mediate LPS insertion across the outer membrane as the LptD transport element; H44/76 surface-accessibility and envelope controls support the native delivery role. The complex contribution does not imply that LptE is obligatory in every context.

PMID15192148 assays H44/76 directly. UniProt wording “Essential for envelope biogenesis” must not be read as H44/76 viability essentiality: an imp deletion survives, while surface-delivery assays show the mechanistic defect. PAINT target leaf was unavailable; no loss-free lineage conclusion is claimed.

Evidence, preserved source hashes, ontology snapshots and validation are in analysis/module_audits/bacterial_lps_transport/neisseria-consultation/.

family_name: CONSERVED COMPONENT OF ABC TRANSPORTER FOR NATURAL AMINO ACIDS-RELATED
preferred_name: LivG/LivF/LptB-type ABC transporter ATP-binding protein family
summary: This ABC nucleotide-binding-domain family includes both amino-acid uptake motors and LptB-like
  lipid-extraction motors. ATP binding/hydrolysis and coupling to membrane partners are conserved, while
  transported cargo depends on the specific paralog and assembly. Characterized E. coli LptB and related

  DR_2134/Q9RSJ0. Thus both family-wide and unqualified SF10-wide LPS transport claims exceed the current
  evidence. ATPase activity remains a conserved genus, not a complete cargo-selective transporter function.

  supports lipid-extraction machinery, not universal LPS cargo or interchangeability of F and G.'

original_text.interpro/panther/PTHR30189/PTHR30189-rev:
family_id: PANTHER:PTHR30189
family_name: LPS-ASSEMBLY PROTEIN
preferred_name: LptD outer-membrane LPS translocon family
summary: LptD proteins form the outer-membrane barrel and periplasmic entry domain of characterized bacterial
  LPS transport systems. In E. coli, LptD associates with the plug lipoprotein LptE to insert LPS into
  the outer leaflet. Neisseria LptD also supports surface LPS delivery, whereas its LptE partner has a
  non-obligatory assembly role under tested conditions. The family contains homologs in diderms lacking
  canonical LPS, whose transported substrate is unresolved; the conserved barrel architecture does not
  by itself specify LPS cargo.
functional_coherence: MOSTLY_COHERENT
coherence_reason: The single SF1 includes characterized LPS translocons and homologs in non-LPS-producing
  diderms. Cached Q9RWU2 (Deinococcus) and Q9X257 (Thermotoga) prevent a universal native LPS assignment.
  Existing PAINT outer-membrane losses for the two Ricinus-labeled leaves are retained without asserting
  their genomic origin. The family is coherent for LptD-like architecture but substrate/partner scope
  is not uniform evidence.
